  {BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.instIsProbabilityMeasureBoolCubeUniformMeasure}
  {context}
  {boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}
  {pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p032-b001}
There is a constant $K>0$ such that, for every pair of natural numbers $n,k$ with $1\le
k$, every real polynomial $p$ in $n$ variables of total degree at most $k$ whose squared
value has integral $1$ under the product of $n$ standard Gaussian measures, and every
$\varepsilon>0$, one has
\[
\gamma_n\bigl(\{z:|p(z)|\le\varepsilon\}\bigr)\le Kk\,\varepsilon^{1/k},
\]
where $\gamma_n$ denotes that product Gaussian measure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Kolmogorov-distance invariance estimate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.invariance_cdf}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.invariance_cdf}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.kolmogorovDistance, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.has_degree_at_most, BooleanAnalysis.influence}
There is a constant $K>0$ such that, for every $n,k\in\mathbb N$ with $1\le k$, every
function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ of degree at most $k$ and variance exactly $1$, and
every $\varepsilon\ge0$ for which all coordinate influences of $f$ are at most
$\varepsilon$, the Kolmogorov distance between the law of $f$ on the uniform Boolean
cube and the law of its Fourier--Walsh polynomial evaluated on independent standard
Gaussian coordinates is at most
\[
Kk\,\varepsilon^{1/(4k+1)}.
\]
\end{theorem}
